kv: Delaware corporation owned 100% by Northrop Grumman Corporation and consolidated in the public parent's financial statements.

The PTS-G design order did not become a Swarm 1 production award; the distinct PTS-P build path must not erase that loss.; PTS-P launch is planned no earlier than FY2030, leaving a long construction, integration and schedule-risk interval.; GPI design funding does not establish hardware qualification or intercept performance.; QTIME award-lead status does not establish accepted rapid NDI or transfer into a production line.; The public parent reported 84% of 2025 sales to the U.S. government, creating customer concentration without proving cross-default among the three subsidiary contracts.

The record supports exact-entity recurrence, not reuse of QTIME outputs in the spacecraft or interceptor programs.

Normalize Corp. and Corporation name variants, but do not replace the subsidiary with Northrop Grumman Corporation.; Do not infer that QTIME equipment, personnel or data are used on PTS-P or GPI without a named technical bridge.; A PTS-G competition result is distinct from the PTS-P contract and must remain attached to the correct program clock.

A production-and-successor prime position in sovereign GPS, reinforced by separate strategic hypersonic, missile-defense and installed shipboard-laser integration roles.

The 2025 Form 10-K reports supplier disruptions that have caused delays and increased costs and are expected to continue in 2026.; GPS IIIF integration and on-orbit acceptance remain later clocks despite GPS III heritage.; Hypersonic and NGI prime status does not establish repeat all-up-round success, qualified production or a successful intercept.; HELIOS installation and training do not disclose operational-effectiveness, availability, formal acceptance or a second ship.; Aculight's adverse IFPC history belongs to Lockheed Martin Aculight Corp. and cannot be attributed to the parent edges without a demonstrated common cause.

No common technical architecture across those programs is proven.

Do not merge Lockheed Martin Corporation with Lockheed Martin Aculight Corp.; The parent Exhibit 21 lists only significant subsidiaries and expressly omits others; absence is not a dissolution or ownership finding.; A program-local test failure cannot propagate to GPS, hypersonics, NGI and HELIOS absent a parent-wide eligibility, common-component, facility or supplier event.

The canonical GPS, hypersonics and missile-defense, and HELIOS edges name Lockheed Martin Corporation. Lockheed Martin Aculight Corp. is a separate canonical legal entity on directed-energy awards and adverse IFPC history and is excluded from this dossier's edge set. The current Exhibit 21 omits non-significant subsidiaries, so omission of Aculight is not evidence that it ceased to exist or can be collapsed into the parent.
